title: A Fully Preoperative CT-Based Nomogram for Predicting Clinically Relevant Postoperative Pancreatic Fistula After Pancreaticoduodenectomy:  Development and Internal Validation in a 17-Year Single-Center Cohort
content: Background/Objectives: Clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (CR-POPF) remains a major complication after pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD). We aimed to develop and internally validate a fully preoperative prediction model using clinical and computed tomography (CT) variables. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 185 patients undergoing PD between 2007 and 2023. CR-POPF was defined according to the 2016 ISGPS criteria. A logistic regression model incorporating body mass index (BMI), main pancreatic duct (MPD) diameter, pancreatic attenuation, and subcutaneous fat area (SFA), all as continuous predictors, was developed. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap resamples, followed by coefficient shrinkage and intercept recalibration. Results: CR-POPF occurred in 26 patients (14.1%). The model included 176 complete cases and 25 events. Adjusted odds ratios were 1.46 (95% CI 1.17–1.82) for BMI, 0.74 (0.57–0.96) for MPD diameter, 0.65 (0.50–0.83) for pancreatic attenuation, and 0.78 (0.65–0.92) for SFA. Apparent and optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.902 (95% CI 0.852–0.953) and 0.891 (approximate 95% CI 0.840–0.952), respectively, with a corrected calibration slope of 0.919. Conclusions: This fully preoperative nomogram demonstrated promising discrimination. However, predictor selection was exploratory and was not repeated during bootstrap validation. External validation is required before clinical implementation.
